title: Cartesian extension of an equivariant marked nodal tower
statement:
Let $k\subseteq e\subseteq F$ be finite field extensions, let $J\twoheadrightarrow G$ be a surjection of finite groups, and let their actions on the fields and schemes below be compatible (actions may be nonfaithful and semilinear). Let $B,V$ be integral finite-type $e$-schemes. Suppose $v:V\to B$ is H-projective, flat and finitely presented, with nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric fibres of pure dimension one, smooth geometrically integral generic fibre, and finitely many disjoint sections $s_j$ in its smooth locus, whose union is $G$-stable. Suppose $v$ is quasi-split: all singular points of every fibre and their two inverse images in its normalization are rational over the base residue field. This is the condition of [def-sfb-quasi-split-nodal-fibres]. Let $D\subset B$ be a $G$-stable nowhere dense closed subset, with $v$ smooth over $B\setminus D$.
Let $P=T_r\to\cdots\to T_0=\operatorname{Spec}F$ be a tower of integral finite-type $F$-schemes with compatible $J$-action. Assume its maps $f_i$ have all the curve, section and quasi-split properties just imposed on $v$. Set $Z_0=\varnothing$ and $Z_i=f_i^{-1}Z_{i-1}\cup\bigcup_\nu s_{i\nu}(T_{i-1})$; assume each $f_i$ is smooth over $T_{i-1}\setminus Z_{i-1}$ and each union of sections is $J$-stable. Let $h:P\to B$ be an equivariant $e$-morphism that is H-projective surjective dominant morphism with $h^{-1}D\subseteq Z_r$. Assume the ordinary fibre product $W=V\times_B P$ is integral, with $k(W)/k(V)$ finite. Let $C,X$ be integral finite-type $k$-schemes and $c:V\to C$, $\pi:C\to X$ equivariant H-projective surjective $k$-morphisms. Let $Z\subset X$ be invariant closed with $c^{-1}\pi^{-1}Z\subseteq v^{-1}D\cup\bigcup_j s_j(B)$. Suppose $k(V)/k(C)$ is finite and $\pi$ is birational.
Then $W\to P$ with the pulled-back sections extends the given tower by one stage, with diagonal $J$-action and all the same curve, section, smoothness and quasi-split properties. Its boundary $Z_{r+1}=\operatorname{pr}_P^{-1}Z_r\cup\bigcup_j s'_j(P)$ is $J$-stable and contains $a^{-1}Z$ for $a=\pi c\operatorname{pr}_V$. The map $a:W\to X$ is equivariant H-projective and surjective and induces a finite extension of function fields. It is also projective in the projective-bundle convention. No assertion of regularity of $W$ or trivial action on sections is made.

Nodal fibres use [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres], and normalization uses [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. H-projective means a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target [def-kun-projective]; the other projectivity convention is [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Fields, extensions, integral schemes, finite type, flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, geometric integrality, geometric fibres, sections, fibre products and function fields use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-field-tower], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-sc-function-field] and [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Birational means an isomorphism over dense opens inducing equality of function fields.

proof.text: Write $p:W\to P$ and $q:W\to V$. For $\gamma\in J$, let $\bar\gamma$ be its image in $G$. Compatibility gives $v\bar\gamma_Vq=\bar\gamma_Bvq=\bar\gamma_Bhp=h\gamma_Pp$. The fibre-product universal property therefore defines a unique $\gamma_W$ with $q\gamma_W=\bar\gamma_Vq$ and $p\gamma_W=\gamma_Pp$. Applying uniqueness to both projections proves $1_W=\mathrm{id}_W$ and $(\gamma\delta)_W=\gamma_W\delta_W$; inverses follow as well. This is a scheme action, semilinear over the given action on $F$, and both projections are equivariant. The same universal property defines $s'_j=(s_jh,\mathrm{id}_P):P\to W$, with $ps'_j=\mathrm{id}_P$.

source.place: Situation 5.8, pp.615--616; Theorem 5.9 proof, p.617, final fibre-product paragraph (primary publisher scan read online; local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Apply the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-marked-nodal-boundary-control] to the family $v$ over the field $e$ and to $h:P\to B$. To check that lemma's other hypotheses one may take its auxiliary invariant closed subset of $V$ to be empty: its generic-fibre containment is then vacuous. All its family and marking hypotheses are exactly those assumed here. In particular quasi-split means the rational-node and two-rational-branch condition of [def-sfb-quasi-split-nodal-fibres], without a smooth-component hypothesis. Its conclusion gives H-projectivity, flatness and finite presentation of $p$, nonempty connected reduced nodal geometric fibres of pure dimension one, quasi-split fibres, and disjoint pulled-back sections in the relative smooth locus. We use only its persistence clause; we do not replace the given $D$ by the exceptional subset it constructs. Moreover $p$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Composing it with the given finite-type structure morphism $P\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ using [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) makes $W$ a finite-type $F$-scheme, as required for the new stage. Properness also includes separatedness. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion] makes each new section a closed immersion. Apply the same properness and section lemmas to each old H-projective $f_i$ as well; their section images are closed. Induction from $Z_0=\varnothing$ by finite unions and inverse images proves that all old boundaries and $Z_{r+1}$ are closed.

source.place: Situation 5.8, pp.615--616; Theorem 5.9 proof, p.617, final fibre-product paragraph (primary publisher scan read online; local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Put $U=B\setminus D$ and $P_U=h^{-1}U$. The morphism $p$ over $P_U$ is the base change of the smooth morphism $V_U\to U$, hence is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Since $h^{-1}D\subseteq Z_r$, this proves smoothness over $P\setminus Z_r$. For the generic fibre, dominance of $h$ between integral schemes gives $h(\eta_P)=\eta_B$ and the canonical field inclusion $k(B)\to k(P)$ of [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. The universal property identifies $W_{\eta_P}$ with $V_{\eta_B}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k(B)}\operatorname{Spec}k(P)$, so the same smooth-base-change lemma proves it smooth. It is geometrically integral directly from the definition: for every field extension $L/k(P)$ its scalar extension is $V_{\eta_B}\times_{k(B)}L$, which is integral by geometric integrality of $V_{\eta_B}$. Thus appending $p$ preserves every family property; $W$ itself is integral by hypothesis.

source.place: Situation 5.8, pp.615--616; Theorem 5.9 proof, p.617, final fibre-product paragraph (primary publisher scan read online; local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Let $M=\bigcup_j s_j(B)$ and $M'=\bigcup_j s'_j(P)$. For each section its inverse-image subscheme $s_j(B)\times_B P$ is precisely the image of $s'_j$, by the universal property and $vs_j=\mathrm{id}_B$; consequently $q^{-1}M=M'$. Since $M$ is $G$-stable and $q$ equivariant, $M'$ is $J$-stable. Induction on the displayed boundary formula for the old tower shows each $Z_i$ is $J$-stable: inverse images along an equivariant map and unions of stable sets are stable, starting at $Z_0=\varnothing$. Therefore $Z_{r+1}=p^{-1}Z_r\cup M'$ is $J$-stable. Pulling back the assumed containment on $V$ gives $a^{-1}Z\subseteq q^{-1}(v^{-1}D\cup M)=p^{-1}(h^{-1}D)\cup M'\subseteq Z_{r+1}$. This is a set-theoretic boundary calculation, with no claim that reduced closed subschemes commute with base change.

source.place: Situation 5.8, pp.615--616; Theorem 5.9 proof, p.617, final fibre-product paragraph (primary publisher scan read online; local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: The projection $q$ is the base change of $h$ along $v$ (interchanging the two factors via their universal properties). To apply [lem-pc-projective-base-change] in its exact convention, first [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] makes the assumed H-projective $h$ proper. Properness includes finite type, which includes quasi-compactness by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Hence $h$ is projective in the convention [def-pc-projective-morphism], namely H-projective and quasi-compact. The cited projective-base-change lemma now makes $q$ projective in that convention, in particular H-projective.

source.place: Tags 01WF (lemma-H-projective-base-change) and 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper); the quasi-compactness convention of def-pc-projective-morphism.

proof.text: Because $h$ is surjective, its base change $q$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Apply [lem-trf-surjective-morphism-composition] first to $q,c$ and then to $cq,\pi$; this proves surjectivity of $a=\pi cq$. Its equivariance follows by composing the equivariance equations for $q,c,\pi$, using the given surjection $J\to G$ on the latter two. The surjective maps $q,c,\pi$ between integral schemes are dominant, so their canonical function-field inclusions are the pullbacks of generic germs and compose as the maps do.

Birationality of $\pi$ identifies $k(X)$ with $k(C)$ through its induced inclusion, by the definition in the statement. The hypotheses already give finite extensions $k(C)\subseteq k(V)\subseteq k(W)$ through $c,q$. If $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ span $k(V)$ over $k(C)$ and $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ span $k(W)$ over $k(V)$, the $mn$ products $u_iw_j$ span $k(W)$ over $k(C)=k(X)$: expand each coefficient of a $w_j$ in the $u_i$. Thus the extension induced by $a$ is finite. Neither integrality of $W$ nor finiteness of $k(W)/k(V)$ is deduced from a normalization or silently added; both are assumptions of this item.

source.place: Situation 5.8, pp.615--616; Theorem 5.9 proof, p.617, final fibre-product paragraph (primary publisher scan read online; local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: By Step 5, $q$ is H-projective, and $c,\pi$ are H-projective by hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] to $q,c$, then to $cq,\pi$. The result is an H-projective factorization $W\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_X\to X$ of $a$. Together with Steps 6--7 this gives all the claimed properties of $a$ except the comparison of projectivity conventions.

Use [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space] with $S=X$ and $r=N$ to identify $\mathbf P^N_X$ in the factorization of Step 8 with $\operatorname{Proj}_X\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal O_X^{\oplus(N+1)})$. The module $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus(N+1)}$ is quasi-coherent of finite type: on each affine open it is the sheaf associated to the finite free module with its displayed basis. Composing the closed immersion of Step 8 with the inverse of this isomorphism exhibits exactly the projective-bundle factorization of [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. This proves the last projectivity assertion without imposing an ample line bundle on $X$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q129-76f9e63df (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all nine steps and every cited statement in full. Changes since the earlier head 667de3c9a65 (returned for a promotion failure, not mathematics): the statement now names def-sfb-quasi-split-nodal-fibres, which is added to stmt_deps, proof_deps and step 2. That definition gives exactly the inline condition: rational singular points with exactly two rational normalization branches, and no smooth-component hypothesis. So the meaning is unchanged. The steps are correct. Step 1: the diagonal J-action comes from fibre-product uniqueness, and the sections are s'_j=(s_j h, id_P). Step 2: every hypothesis of the boundary-control persistence clause holds with k=e and auxiliary Z empty; that clause holds for any base change and does not replace the given D. H-projective implies proper, hence finite type and separated, so W is of finite type over F and the sections are closed immersions. Step 3: P minus Z_r lies inside h^{-1}(B minus D), so p is smooth there by base change. Dominance gives W over the generic point of P as V over the generic point of B base-changed to k(P), which is smooth and geometrically integral directly from the definition. Step 4: q^{-1}(s_j(B)) equals s'_j(P), and a^{-1}Z lies in p^{-1}h^{-1}D union M', which lies in Z_{r+1}, using vq=hp. Step 5: h is quasi-compact through properness, so the projective-base-change node applies. Steps 6-8: surjectivity by base change and composition; finiteness by the tower k(X)=k(C) in k(V) in k(W); H-projectivity of a by Stacks 01WE twice (checked in local morphisms.tex). Step 9: P^N_X is identified with Proj Sym(O^{N+1}), giving the projective-bundle convention. Edge cases r=0, no sections, D and Z empty, and nonfaithful actions break no step. The de Jong source (Situation 5.8, Theorem 5.9 p.617) has no local copy; it is marked WANTED with an agent-written proof origin, so I could not check the source itself. There are no new nodes and no duplicate statement in the DAG.
